claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release notes: sudo-rs is the default sudo provider; the core utilities are provided by rust-coreutils (GNU cp, mv and rm are still used 'because of unresolved bugs'); the GA kernel moves from 6.8 to 7.0; Dracut is the default initial-ramdisk infrastructure, replacing initramfs-tools, which 'remains supported'

Launchpad: rauc 1.15.1-1 is published in Ubuntu 26.04 'resolute' release pocket, component universe (published 2026-01-20); 1.13-3 was superseded in resolute on 2025-10-09; no rauc in resolute-updates or -security

RAUC v1.13 requires the dm-verity table status to equal exactly 'V'; Linux commit ae97648e (2025-11-05, in v6.19-rc1) adds a second status field (FEC-corrected block count, '-' when FEC is off), so on Linux >= 6.19 RAUC 1.13 cannot mount any verity bundle ('Unexpected dm-verity status 'V -''). Upstream fix a45cdb14 (with preparatory abeccdc5, a40986fe; src/dm.c only) is first released in RAUC 1.15.1 (2026-01-05); v1.14 and v1.15 do not contain it (rauc issue #1842)
version: RAUC v1.13 / fix in v1.15.1; Linux v6.19-rc1

claim: Debian 13 ships rauc 1.13-3+deb13u1 (patches: two signature fixes for CVE-2026-34155, OpenSSL 3.5 test fixes, library reinit; not the dm-verity status fix), with no rauc in trixie-backports; forky/sid have 1.15.2-1. trixie-backports publishes linux-signed-amd64 from 6.16 up to 7.2.12, so Debian 13 + a backports kernel >= 6.19 + Debian's RAUC hits the same failure as C-LAB-ubuntu-2604-leg-003 [inference from -003 and the package metadata; not run in the lab]

Lab (Ubuntu 26.04.1 minbase amd64, build day 2026-11-11): kernel 7.0.0-43-generic via linux-image-virtual; i6300esb watchdog module is in the base linux-modules package; 'date' is uutils coreutils 0.10.0 (rust-coreutils 0.10.0-1ubuntu2~26.04.1); the kernel package Recommends 'dracut | linux-initramfs-tool', so initramfs-tools had to be named explicitly to keep Debian's boot path; minbase installs neither snapd nor apparmor nor sudo; rootfs 790 MiB (archive RAUC) / 805 MiB (RAUC built from source) including k3s and its air-gap images

Lab: the Debian gate files (onemind-health-gate, onemind-k3s-check, RAUC pre-install handler, units, manifests, bad-hang init, API stand-in), the GRUB template and the generated grub.cfg ran on Ubuntu 26.04 byte-identical (13 files hashed); only bootstrap/package lines of the build changed. The gate's shell scripts ran correctly under uutils coreutils

Lab: Ubuntu 26.04's systemd 259 emits OSC 3008 'context' escape sequences (with a fresh UUID) around every shell prompt and command on the serial console; Debian 13's systemd 257.13 emitted none. A console-scraping test driver must strip them across read boundaries; the original driver's per-read stripping also intermittently missed short CSI sequences on Debian under host load

Lab: with systemd-logind masked (as in the Debian image), 'systemctl reboot' on Ubuntu 26.04 prints 'Call to Reboot failed: Unit dbus-org.freedesktop.login1.service failed to load properly' but the system still reboots; every reboot in the battery completed

Home Assistant OS at ab7d0f1 (2026-11-10): generic_x86_64 defconfig pins kernel 6.18.62 (BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_VERSION_VALUE) and enables RAUC from its Buildroot fork (home-assistant/buildroot@5c344b3: RAUC_VERSION = 1.13, plus 0001-fix-cve-2026-34155.patch), with one extra HAOS patch (buildroot-external/patches/rauc/0001-src-event_log-add-SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER...); no dm-verity status fix, so HAOS stays compatible only while its kernel is < 6.19 [inference for the last clause, from C-LAB-ubuntu-2604-leg-003]

Lab: on Ubuntu 26.04 (kernel 7.0.0-43-generic), upstream RAUC v1.13 (1183a39, the version Debian 13 ships) fails every 'rauc install' of a verity bundle with 'Failed mounting bundle: Unexpected dm-verity status 'V -' (instead of '\0')' before writing any slot; the box stays on its committed slot (U1 run 1, T3)

Lab: Ubuntu 26.04 with Ubuntu's rauc 1.15.1-1 and the unchanged OneMind fresh-signal k3s gate passed T1-T9 and T10r of the LAB-rauc-k3s-gate battery in two complete runs (U2 runs 3 and 4, driver exit 0; same verdicts as Debian 13): good update committed only after 3 fresh passes, broken-k3s and stale-Ready updates rolled back at the 300 s deadline, panic and hang each tried 3 times then marked bad, power cuts during write and during the commit window recovered without input; the naive gate (T10) committed a broken system in every run [TCG emulation, not hardware]

Lab: RAUC v1.13 plus only the three upstream src/dm.c commits abeccdc5, a40986fe, a45cdb14 passed the full battery on Ubuntu 26.04 (U1p run 1: T1, T3-T9, T10r PASS; T2 PASS in a separate driver-fixed check run), so the dm-verity status check was the only Ubuntu-specific blocker for RAUC 1.13

Lab (paired run, same second, same lab VM, no other guest): Debian 13 vs Ubuntu 26.04 images with the same gate: k3s fresh on first boot after 136 s vs 148 s; good update committed after 120 s vs 122 s; no Ubuntu slowdown on the update path beyond run-to-run noise [one paired sample, TCG emulation; single-run differences up to ~2x were host load]
